statement.text:
The mapping class group of a closed, orientable, genus $g$ sur-
face $S$ acts by symplectomorphisms on the symmetric product $\operatorname{Sym}^{g}(S)$. In partic-
ular, it acts smoothly on $\operatorname{Sym}^{g}(S)$.
(a) What is the kernel of the map from the mapping class group of $S$ to the
smooth mapping class group of $\operatorname{Sym}^{g}(S)$? What about in the based case?
(b) Given disjoint simple closed curves $\alpha_{1},..., \alpha_{g}$ in $S$, there is a correspond-
ing torus $T_{\alpha}$ in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g}(S)$: the image of $\alpha_{1} \times \cdots \times \alpha_{g} \subset S^{g}$. These are
the tori that appear in Heegaard Floer theory. When do $\alpha_{1},..., \alpha_{g}$ and
$\beta_{1},..., \beta_{g}$ give smoothly isotopic tori? When are they Lagrangian isotopic
for an appropriate choice of symplectic form?
